title: Isaac Shelby, "Old Kings Mountain"
summary: Maryland-born Isaac Shelby, hero of Kings Mountain in 1780, became Kentucky's first governor in 1792 and led its volunteers at the Thames in 1813.
bodyMarkdown:
Shelby County's namesake was a frontier celebrity before Kentucky was a state. [Isaac Shelby](/people/#isaac-shelby) was born in Maryland in 1750 and grew up on the Virginia–Tennessee frontier, where his father Evan Shelby was a militia captain.

In 1774 young Isaac served in his father's company at the Battle of Point Pleasant in Lord Dunmore's War, under [Andrew Lewis](/people/#andrew-lewis). The Shawnee leader [Cornstalk](/stories/cornstalk-hokoleskwa-point-pleasant-to-fort-randolph/) led the other side. The next year Shelby came into Kentucky as a surveyor and marked a claim of his own.

The fight that gave him his nickname came in the Carolinas. On October 7, 1780, Shelby, John Sevier, William Campbell, and other colonels led the [Overmountain Men](https://grokipedia.com/page/Overmountain_Men) against a Loyalist force on a ridge just inside South Carolina. The [Battle of Kings Mountain](https://grokipedia.com/page/Battle_of_Kings_Mountain) lasted about an hour. The Loyalist commander, Patrick Ferguson, was killed, and nearly his whole force was killed or captured. It was a turning point in the war in the South, and the men who won it were backcountry riflemen like the ones settling Kentucky.

Shelby moved to Kentucky for good in the 1780s. He married [Susannah Hart](/people/#susannah-shelby) in 1783 and built a stone house, Traveler's Rest, in what was then Lincoln County. He sat in the conventions that argued for statehood, and in 1792 the electors chose him, without a dissenting vote, as the commonwealth's first governor. Shelby County, formed from Jefferson County that year, was named for him.

He went home to farming after one term. Then the [War of 1812](/stories/river-raisin-1813-kentuckys-winter-defeat-in-michigan/) brought him back. Kentuckians elected him governor again in 1812, and in 1813, at sixty-three, he led thousands of Kentucky volunteers north. At the [Battle of the Thames](https://grokipedia.com/page/Battle_of_the_Thames) in Upper Canada that October, mounted Kentuckians under [Richard M. Johnson](/people/#richard-m-johnson) broke the British line, and the Shawnee leader Tecumseh was killed.

In 1818 Shelby and Andrew Jackson negotiated the Chickasaw treaty that brought the Jackson Purchase into Kentucky. He died at Traveler's Rest in 1826.

## Kentucky today

Shelby is buried at the Isaac Shelby Cemetery State Historic Site in Boyle County, on the grounds of his old farm. [Shelbyville](/stories/shelbyville/), the seat of the county named for him, keeps his name on the map.
